issue: Both Wikivoyage quotes verified verbatim. Wiktionary and Jisho confirm ありがとう = thank you (arigatō); Jisho marks arigatō gozaimasu as polite (teineigo), supporting explain. Distractors clearly wrong.

Quotes verified on Wikivoyage. Wiktionary confirms お願いします (onegai shimasu) = 'Please' (request) and lists dōzo for offering. Minor: kudasai is another request 'please' that the accept list does not include, but no distractor is arguably correct.
Wikivoyage '1 一 / 壱 (ichi)' and Wikipedia table row (ichi, hito(tsu), preferred ichi) both verified; hitotsu also on Wikivoyage native-count list.
Wikivoyage and Wikipedia agree: 三 san, kun mit(tsu); mittsu in Wikivoyage native-count list.

Wikivoyage '4 四 (yon or shi)' and superstition note verified; Wikipedia 'yon (4) and nana (7) are preferred' and 'It is purported...death' verified. 'reportedly' hedge preserved. shi not among distractors.
Wikivoyage '7 七 (nana or shichi)' and Wikipedia table row/preference sentence verified. 'shichi common when counting' is from Wikivoyage only.
Wikivoyage '9 九 (kyū)' and Wikipedia row (ku, kyū; preferred kyū) verified; accepting 'ku' is supported as a valid reading.
Wikivoyage '10 十 / 拾 (jū)', Wikipedia row and 'Tens from 20 to 90...ni-jū' all verified; Wikivoyage also lists 20 = ni-jū.
Wikivoyage 'What? 何？ Nani?' and 'Kore wa nan desu ka?' verified. Wiktionary 何: read なに, but なん before だ/で/の, supporting the nan-before-desu note.
Wikivoyage Who?/Dore?/Anata wa dare desu ka quotes verified. Wiktionary 誰 (だれ, dare) = who; lists dore separately as 'which'.
Wikivoyage 'I don't understand. 分かりません。 Wakarimasen.' verified; Wiktionary: polite negative of wakaru (understand). Distractors (sumimasen, hanasemasen, irimasen) clearly different meanings.

Both Wikivoyage quotes verified; Wikivoyage also gives itadakimasu 'when starting a meal'. Wiktionary ごちそうさまでした = 'it was delicious' (ご馳走様でした). Short form 'gochisōsama' in accept is a casual equivalent.
